item.title: Again 2018? The Tables Have Turned Between Trump and Kim Jong-un (어게인 2018? 트럼프와 김정은 갑을이 바뀌었다)
item.description:
Again 2018? The Tables Have Turned Between Trump and Kim Jong-un (어게인 2018? 트럼프와 김정은 갑을이 바뀌었다)

Attention is focused on a U.S.-North Korea summit as President Trump announced he would meet North Korean Chairman Kim Jong-un within this year. Trump reiterated his intention to pursue a meeting with Kim within the year, saying, "The fact that I get along well with Kim Jong-un is not a bad thing—it's a good thing." (트럼프 대통령이 올해 안에 북한 김정은 국무위원장을 만날 것이라고 밝히면서 미·북 정상회담에 관심이 집중되고 있습니다. 트럼프 대통령은 “내가 김정은과 잘 지낸다는 사실은 나쁜 게 아니라 좋은 일”이라며 연내 김정은과 회담 추진 의사를 거듭 밝혔습니다.)

The government has welcomed Trump's initiative toward North Korea with open arms. President Lee Jae-myung praised it as "a major decision reflecting deep thought aimed at moving beyond hostility and confrontation to build peace on the Korean Peninsula." He also said, "I look forward to reuniting with President Trump in the United States before long." This appears to hint at a meeting with Trump during international events such as the UN General Assembly scheduled for late September. (트럼프의 대북 구상에 정부는 적극 환영 입장을 밝혔습니다. 이재명 대통령은 “한반도에서 적대와 대결을 넘어 평화를 만들기 위한 고심이 담긴 큰 결정”이라고 평가했습니다. 또 “머지않아 미국에서 트럼프 대통령과의 재회를 기대한다”고도 했습니다. 9월 하순에 예정된 유엔 총회 등 국제 행사 때 트럼프와 만남을 암시한 듯합니다.)

It is also read as a willingness to not only support the U.S.-North Korea talks from behind but also step forward as a mediator to facilitate U.S.-North Korea dialogue. At last year's South Korea-U.S. summit held at the White House, President Lee called Trump a "peace maker" and said he would play the role of a "pace maker." (미·북 회담을 뒤에서 지원하는 것은 물론이고 미·북 대화를 촉진하는 중재자로 나서겠다는 의지로도 읽힙니다. 이 대통령은 작년 백악관에서 열린 한미 정상회담에서 트럼프 대통령을 ‘피스 메이커’로 칭하면서 자신은 ‘페이스 메이커’ 역할을 하겠다고 했습니다.)

Through Trump's initiative for a U.S.-North Korea summit, the government appears to expect that a inter-Korean-U.S. dialogue phase, similar to that of eight years ago, will open again. Within the government and the ruling party, the phrase "Trump-initiated Again 2018" is being floated. It is read as a plan to break through the inter-Korean relations that have been completely blocked by North Korea's "hostile two-state" stance and to pursue peace negotiations among South Korea, North Korea, the U.S., and China. (정부는 이번 트럼프의 미·북 정상회담 구상을 통해 8년 전과 같은 남·북·미 대화 국면이 다시 열릴 것을 기대하고 있는 듯합니다. 정부와 여권 내부에선 ‘트럼프 발(發) 어게인 2018’이란 말이 나옵니다. 북한의 ‘적대적 2국가’ 기조로 인해 꽉 막혔던 남북관계를 뚫고 남·북·미·중 간 평화 협상도 추진하려는 구상으로 읽힙니다.)

However, there are many observations that this Trump-initiated U.S.-North Korea meeting will differ from the first U.S.-North Korea summit held in Singapore in 2018. First of all, North Korea's internal situation, the international landscape, and the level of nuclear development have changed beyond comparison with eight years ago. In 2018, the U.S. was the relaxed superior party and North Korea was the anxious inferior, but now it is different. There is a high possibility that North Korea will no longer be dragged along by the U.S. In fact, talk has emerged that the tables have turned. (하지만 이번 트럼프발 미·북 회담은 2018년 싱가포르에서 열린 1차 미·북 정상회담과는 다를 것이라는 관측이 많습니다. 우선 북한의 내부 상황와 국제 정세, 핵 개발 수준이 8년 전과는 비교할 수 없을 정도로 달라졌습니다. 2018년에는 미국이 느긋한 갑(甲)이었고, 북한이 다급한 을(乙)이었지만 지금은 다릅니다. 북한이 더 이상 미국에 끌려다니지 않을 가능성이 큽니다. 오히려 갑을이 바뀌었다는 얘기까지 나옵니다.)

North Korea has continuously expanded its production of nuclear materials and the number of warheads. Intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) and submarine-launched ballistic missiles (SLBMs) targeting South Korea and the U.S., as well as short- and medium-range ballistic missiles and large-caliber multiple rocket launchers, are becoming increasingly advanced and precise. It is effectively moving toward the completion stage of nuclear development. The U.S. is now in a position where it can no longer prevent North Korea's nuclear development through negotiations. (북한은 그동안 핵 물질 생산과 탄두 숫자를 지속적으로 늘려왔습니다. 한국과 미국을 겨냥한 대륙간탄도미사일(ICBM)과 잠수함발사탄도미사일(SLBM), 중단거리 탄도 미사일, 대형 방사포도 갈수록 고도화 정밀화하고 있습니다. 사실상 핵 개발 완성 단계로 나아가고 있습니다. 미국으로선 더 이상 협상을 통해 북한 핵 개발을 막기 힘든 상황에 처해 있습니다.)

North Korea's international standing and economic situation are also different from eight years ago. North Korea has used its troop deployment to the Ukraine war and the U.S.-China conflict to grow closer to China and Russia. Through this, it is assessed to have largely overcome international sanctions and diplomatic isolation. Backed by China and Russia, it has reached a position where it can even talk loudly to the U.S. Kim Yo-jong's reserved response to Trump's push for a U.S.-North Korea summit, saying it is "something I know little about," vividly illustrates this situation. It appears as though she is brushing off Trump's courtship. (북한의 국제적 위상과 경제 사정도 8년 전과는 다릅니다. 북한은 우크라이나 전쟁 파병과 미·중 갈등 상황을 이용해 중·러와 밀착하고 있습니다. 이를 통해 국제 제재와 외교적 고립도 상당부분 타개한 것으로 평가됩니다. 중·러의 뒷배를 믿고 미국에 되레 큰소리 칠 수 있는 입장이 됐다는 것입니다. 김여정이 트럼프의 미·북 회담 추진에 대해 “잘 알지 못하는 일”이라고 유보적인 반응을 보인 것은 이 같은 상황을 단적으로 보여줍니다. 트럼프의 구애를 튕긴 듯한 모습입니다.)

Trump, on the other hand, is currently mired in the Iran war. His approval ratings are steadily declining. The congressional midterm elections are also waiting in early September. It is a time when a change of mood is needed. Trump appears to be trying to use the U.S.-North Korea summit as that breakthrough. Hence the impression that he is emphasizing his friendship with Kim Jong-un and pushing hard for a summit. (반면 트럼프는 지금 이란 전쟁의 늪에 빠져 있습니다. 국정 지지율은 갈수록 하락하고 있습니다. 9월 초 의회 중간선거도 기다리고 있습니다. 국면 전환이 필요한 시점입니다. 트럼프는 미·북 정상회담을 그 돌파구로 활용하려는 듯합니다. 그래서 김정은과 친분을 강조하며 정상회담을 밀어붙이는 인상입니다.)

Trump appears anxious, while Kim Jong-un seems relaxed. Trump's first-time disclosure that "North Korea has 57 nuclear weapons" is also significant. It appears as an attempt to coax Kim into coming to the table by signaling willingness to recognize North Korea as a nuclear-weapon state. The atmosphere between the U.S. and North Korea has reversed 180 degrees from 2018. (트럼프는 다급하고 오히려 김정은이 느긋한 모양새입니다. 트럼프 대통령이 “북한 핵이 57개”라고 처음 공개한 것도 의미심장합니다. 김정은을 향해 핵보유국으로 인정해 줄 테니 회담에 나오라고 회유하는 것처럼 비칩니다. 미·북 간 분위기가 2018년과 180도 달라진 것입니다.)

Kim Yo-jong poured scornful criticism at our government. She said, "It has fallen into a pitiful predicament of having to pack up the war games it enjoyed the most at the mere word of Trump." Toward President Lee, she said, "His double-dealing words and actions perfectly reveal South Korea's anxious and restless contradictory psychology." She also launched around ten short-range ballistic missiles in a salvo, as if mocking the reduction of ROK-U.S. exercises. (김여정은 우리 정부를 향해 조롱섞인 비판을 쏟아냈습니다. “트럼프의 말 한마디에 제일 즐겨하던 전쟁놀이판을 거둬야 하는 가긍한 처지가 됐다”는 것입니다. 이 대통령을 향해선 “이중적 언행은 한국의 불안 초조한 모순 심리를 그대로 보여준다”고 했습니다. 한미 훈련 축소를 비웃듯 단거리 탄도미사일 10여발을 무더기로 발사하기도 했습니다.)

President Trump did not consult our government at all regarding his push for a meeting with Kim Jong-un. The sudden reduction of ROK-U.S. joint exercises was also carried out without any prior consultation. Our diplomatic and military authorities knew nothing about it. As an ally, we were bypassed on both the talks and the exercises. (트럼프 대통령은 김정은과 회담 추진에 대해 우리 정부와 한 마디 상의도 하지 않았습니다. 갑작스런 한미 연합 훈련 축소도 사전 협의가 전혀 없었습니다. 우리 외교·군 당국은 이를 전혀 알지 못했습니다. 동맹국인데 회담도 훈련도 패싱당한 것입니다.)

President Trump has criticized our lack of cooperation on the Iran war. Complaints about delays in investment in the U.S. are also surfacing in many places. Experts observe that the likelihood of Trump, who is pushing for a summit with Kim Jong-un, closely coordinating with our government is not high. (트럼프 대통령은 이란 전쟁에 대한 우리의 비협조를 비판해 왔습니다. 대미 투자 지연에 대한 불만도 곳곳에서 터져나옵니다. 그런 트럼프가 김정은과 정상회담을 추진하면서 우리 정부와 긴밀하게 협의를 할 가능성은 높지 않다는 게 전문가들 관측입니다.)

Our government expects to play the role of mediator or pace maker for the U.S.-North Korea summit. But North Korea treats us with hostility and is pursuing a strategy of engaging the U.S. while shutting out the South. Trump also has considerable reason to exclude South Korea from North Korea negotiations due to grievances over Iran and delayed U.S. investment. In such a case, far from mediating, we may struggle even to serve as a mere backdrop at the Trump-Kim meeting. (우리 정부는 미·북 정상회담의 중재자나 페이스 메이커 역할을 기대하고 있습니다. 하지만 북한은 우리를 적대시하며 통미봉남 전략을 펴고 있습니다. 트럼프도 이란·대미투자 불만 때문에 한국을 대북 협상에서 제외시킬 가능성이 적잖습니다. 이럴 경우 중재는 커녕 트럼프와 김정은 회담의 들러리 서는 것조차 힘들 수 있습니다.)

If Trump unilaterally agrees at a meeting with Kim Jong-un to reduce U.S. troops in South Korea, halt ROK-U.S. exercises, or a nuclear freeze in exchange for sanction relief, we could face a fatal security crisis. There are strong concerns that, far from "Again 2018," we could be blindsided while suffering a security bypass. (만일 트럼프가 김정은과 회담에서 일방적으로 주한미군 축소나 한미 훈련 중단, 핵 동결-제재 완화에 합의한다면 우리는 치명적 안보 위기에 봉착할 수 있습니다. ‘어게인 2018’은 커녕 안보 패싱을 당하면서 뒤통수를 맞을 수 있다는 우려가 큽니다.)

A summit between President Trump and Chairman Kim Jong-un within the year is still an undercooked story. But there is clearly a possibility it will materialize. That is because President Trump strongly wants a meeting with Kim Jong-un. (트럼프 대통령와 김정은 위원장 간의 연내 정상회담은 아직 설익은 얘기입니다. 하지만 성사 가능성은 분명히 있습니다. 트럼프 대통령이 김정은과 회담을 강하게 원하기 때문입니다.)

Right now, President Trump is trapped in the quagmire of the Iran war and can barely find his way out. His approval ratings have also fallen to record lows. The congressional midterm elections, which will serve as a midterm assessment of President Trump, are scheduled for November 3. If this trend continues, victory in the election is a distant hope. If he loses, lame-duck status will begin immediately. (지금 트럼프 대통령은 이란 전쟁의 늪에 빠져 좀처럼 헤어나오지 못하고 있습니다. 국정 지지율도 역대 최저치로 떨어졌습니다. 트럼프 대통령에 대한 중간 평가가 될 의회 중간선거가 11월 3일 실시됩니다. 이 추세로 가면 선거 승리는 난망한 일입니다. 만일 진다면 레임덕이 곧바로 시작될 것입니다.)

For Trump, he needs a card to shift the mood and overturn the stalemated Iran issue. The incentive to use the U.S.-North Korea summit as that breakthrough is that much greater. In fact, U.S. media attention has recently been shifting from Iran to North Korea. The question is whether Kim Jong-un will respond in kind. (트럼프로선 교착 상태의 이란 문제를 뒤집을 국면 전환용 카드가 필요합니다. 미북 회담을 그 돌파구로 삼으려할 유인이 그만큼 큽니다. 실제로 최근 미국 언론의 관심은 이란에서 북한으로 옮겨오고 있습니다. 문제는 김정은의 화답 여부입니다.)

However, Kim Yo-jong said of the meeting, "It is something I know absolutely nothing about." She did not reject the U.S.-North Korea summit, but neither did she accept it. Trump said he had been in contact with North Korea, but nothing has been confirmed. Even if contact was made, it has not reached the stage of concrete discussions. (그런데 김여정은 회담에 대해 “전혀 알지 못하는 일”이라고 했습니다. 미북 회담을 거절하진 않았지만 수락한 것도 아닙니다. 트럼프는 북한과 접촉했다고 했지만 확인된 건 없습니다. 설사 접촉을 했다고 해도 구체적 논의까지 간 단계는 아닙니다.)

North Korea's seemingly evasive attitude appears to mean it wants to see what gift Trump will offer. It can be interpreted as a decision to be made after seeing whether Trump will grant recognition as a nuclear-weapon state, sanctions relief, and suspension of ROK-U.S. exercises. From North Korea's perspective, there is no reason to rush a response to Trump's proposal. The longer it drags out and plays push-and-pull, the bigger the gift it can extract. It can also gain the upper hand in negotiations. If a U.S.-North Korea summit does take place, it is highly likely to be at the China APEC meeting scheduled for mid-November. (북한의 튕기는 듯한 태도는 트럼프가 줄 선물이 뭔지 보겠다는 뜻으로 비칩니다. 핵보유국 인정과 제제 완화, 한미훈련 중단 등을 트럼프가 들어줄 지 보고 나서 결정하겠다는 의미로 해석할 수 있습니다. 북으로선 트럼프의 제안에 서둘러 답할 이유가 없습니다. 시간을 끌며 밀당을 할수록 얻어낼 수 있는 선물은 커집니다. 협상에서도 우위에 설 수 있습니다. 만일 미북 회담이 열린다면 11월 중순 예정된 중국 APEC 회의가 될 가능성이 큽니다.)

There are similarities between 2018 and now, but the differences are also significant. The commonality is that the summit was initiated by political motives. Back then, we were just before local elections. Trump also needed a diplomatic achievement. Kim Jong-un needed to escape sanctions and isolation. So it drifted toward a political event rather than substantive nuclear agreement. (2018년과 지금은 닮은점도 있지만 차이점도 큽니다. 공통점은 회담이 정치적 동기로 시작됐다는 것입니다. 당시 우리는 지방선거 직전이었고요. 트럼프도 외교적 업적이 필요한 시점이었습니다. 김정은은 제재와 고립에서 벗어나야 했습니다. 그래서 실질적 핵 합의보다는 정치적 이벤트로 흘렀습니다.)

The atmosphere this time is similar. Trump avoided mentioning North Korean denuclearization, saying, "I don't want to talk about it." Rather than the denuclearization issue, which was difficult to agree on from the start, there is considerable likelihood he is focused only on political deals such as a nuclear freeze and cessation of hostile acts. The way Trump and Kim Jong-un show off their good relationship is also similar. (이번도 비슷한 분위기입니다. 트럼프는 북 비핵화에 대해선 “얘기하고 싶지 않다”며 언급을 피했습니다. 애초부터 합의가 힘든 비핵화 문제 보다는 핵동결과 적대 행위 중단 등 정치적 딜에만 관심을 두고 있을 가능성이 적잖습니다. 트럼프와 김정은이 서로 관계가 좋다고 과시하는 것도 비슷합니다.)

The biggest difference is that the tables have turned between the U.S. and North Korea. Back then, the North was anxious and the U.S. was relatively relaxed. This time, Trump appears eager while Kim Jong-un seems to be playing hard to get. North Korea has already largely escaped sanctions and isolation through its closeness with China and Russia, and its nuclear development is at the completion stage. (가장 큰 차이점은 미북 간 갑을이 바뀌었다는 겁니다. 그 때는 북이 다급했고 미국은 상대적으로 느긋했습니다. 이번엔 트럼프가 급하고 김정은이 튕기는 듯한 모습입니다. 북한은 중·러 밀착으로 이미 제재와 고립에서 상당부분 벗어났고 핵 개발도 완성 단계입니다.)

Another difference is that South Korea's role as mediator in the talks is nowhere to be seen. Eight years ago, South Korea first held dialogue with the North on the nuclear issue and mediated the summit by conveying the North's willingness to denuclearize to Trump. Now, there is a possibility that China, as the host of APEC, will take over that role. (또 하나는 한국의 회담 중재 역할이 전혀 보이지 않는다는 겁니다. 8년 전엔 한국이 북한과 먼저 핵 문제에 대해 대화를 했고, 북측의 비핵화 의사를 트럼프에 전달하며 회담을 중재했습니다. 지금은 APEC 개최국인 중국이 그 역할을 대신할 가능성이 있습니다.)

President Trump has asserted that North Korea has 57 nuclear weapons. It is the first time a U.S. president has specified the number of North Korean nuclear weapons in this manner. It has not been clearly confirmed whether North Korea truly has 57 nuclear weapons. Trump has often misstated important data in the past, such as the number of U.S. troops in South Korea. Nevertheless, there are two presumed reasons he directly mentioned the sensitive number of nuclear weapons. (트럼프 대통령은 북핵이 57개라고 못박았습니다. 미국 대통령이 북한 핵무기 숫자를 이처럼 명시한 것은 처음입니다. 북한 핵무기가 정말 57개인지 명확하게 확인된 것도 아닙니다. 트럼프는 과거에도 주한미군 숫자 등 중요한 데이터를 틀리게 말한 경우가 많습니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 그는 민감한 핵무기 숫자를 직접 언급한 이유는 두 가지로 추정됩니다.)

First, it is aimed at creating a sense of crisis for the U.S. domestic audience. It sounds like he is saying, "This is a dangerous situation where the North has 57 nuclear weapons it can launch at any moment, so I will step in personally and resolve it." Second, it is intended to lure North Korea to the table. It means, "I know the scale of the nuclear weapons Kim Jong-un has, and I am willing to recognize North Korea's nuclear status, so let's meet and talk." (첫째는 미국 내부를 겨냥한 위기감 조성 목적입니다. 북이 당장 쏠 수 있는 핵무기가 57개나 되는 위험한 상황이니 내가 직접 나서서 해결하겠다는 뜻으로 들립니다. 둘째는 북한에 대한 회담 유도용입니다. 김정은이 가진 핵무기 규모를 알고 있고 핵보유도 인정할 용의가 있으니까 만나서 대화하자는 겁니다.)

If a U.S.-North Korea summit does take place, will a nuclear agreement be reached between the two sides? Unfortunately, the likelihood of a denuclearization agreement is very low. For one thing, North Korea has no will whatsoever to denuclearize on its own. The U.S. also cannot accept a lower-level agreement than the Hanoi summit due to domestic sentiment. (만일 미북 회담이 열린다면 양측 간 핵 합의가 이뤄질까요. 불행하게도 비핵화 합의가 이뤄질 가능성은 매우 낮습니다. 일단 북한 스스로 비핵화 의지가 전혀 없습니다. 미국도 하노이 회담 때보다 낮은 수준의 합의는 국민정서 상 힘듭니다.)

There are projections of a "small deal" where the U.S. would ease some sanctions in exchange for a nuclear freeze or a halt to ICBM development. However, since North Korea is already evading sanctions through China and Russia, this possibility is also assessed as not very high. Finally, there is the possibility of a political deal involving cessation of mutual hostilities and improved relations. In that case, there would be no deal on nuclear weapons, and it could end as a photo-op political show. Kim Jong-un would seek to elevate his domestic and international standing through such a process and gain recognition of his status as a nuclear-weapon state. (북핵 동결이나 ICBM 개발 중단을 대가로 미국이 일부 제재를 풀어주는 스몰딜로 갈 거란 전망도 나습니다. 하지만 북한이 이미 중·러를 통해 제재를 피하고 있어서 이 가능성도 아주 높진 않다는 평가입니다. 마지막으로 상호 적대시 중단과 관계 개선 등 정치적 딜 가능성인데요. 이 경우 핵은 노딜이고, 정치적 사진찍기 쇼에 그칠 수 있습니다. 김정은은 이런 과정을 통해 자신의 국내·외적 위상을 높이고 핵 보유국으로서 지위를 인정받으려 할 것입니다.)

The government is welcoming the U.S.-North Korea summit. President Lee himself called it "a major decision for peace on the Korean Peninsula." The government is also not hiding its expectations. It said it pays respect even to the reduction of ROK-U.S. exercises for the sake of the U.S.-North Korea summit. (정부는 미북 회담을 환영하고 있습니다. 이 대통령이 직접 “한반도 평화를 위한 큰 결정”이라고 했고요. 정부도 기대감을 감추지 않고 있습니다. 미북 회담을 위해 한미 훈련을 축소하는 것에 대해서도 경의를 표한다고 했습니다.)

However, there is considerable likelihood this will remain nothing more than our one-sided expectations and hopes. Trump has neither consulted nor notified us about the U.S.-North Korea summit or the suspension of ROK-U.S. exercises. There is a high chance he will deal directly with Kim Jong-un, leaving us out. If the impulsive and alliance-dismissive Trump unilaterally agrees with the North on reducing U.S. troops in South Korea, halting ROK-U.S. exercises, or a nuclear freeze, it could be a security catastrophe for us. Trump recently expressed outright dissatisfaction with South Korea's non-cooperation on the Iran issue and delays in investment in the U.S. (하지만 이는 우리의 일방적 기대와 희망에 그칠 가능성이 적잖습니다. 트럼프는 미북 회담이나 한미 훈련 중단에 대해 아무런 협의도 통보도 하지 않았습니다. 김정은과 회담도 우리는 빼고 직거래할 가능성이 큽니다. 즉흥적이고 동맹을 무시하는 트럼프가 북한과 일방적으로 주한미군 감축이나 한미훈련 중단, 핵동결 합의를 한다면 우리에겐 안보 재앙이 될 수 있습니다. 트럼프는 최근 한국의 이란 문제 비협조와 대미 투자 지연에 대해 노골적 불만을 표시했습니다.)

North Korea also mocked our government, calling it "a pitiful and pathetic situation." It criticized President Lee as well for "double-dealing words and actions" and "anxious and restless psychology." It also launched a salvo of short-range ballistic missiles targeting us. There is no sign at all that it will change its hostile policy toward the South. Such a North Korea is unlikely to welcome our role as mediator or pace maker. It will come out with a strategy of engaging the U.S. while excluding and shutting out the South, dealing thoroughly and directly with the U.S. (북한도 우리 정부를 향해 “가엽고 불쌍한 처지”라고 조롱했습니다. 이 대통령에 대해서도 “이중 언행” “불안 초조한 심리”라고 비판했습니다. 우리를 겨냥해 단거리 탄도미사일도 무더기 발사했습니다. 대남 적대시 정책을 바꿀 기미가 전혀 없습니다. 이런 북한이 우리의 중재역, 페이스 메이커 역할을 반길 리 없습니다. 한국은 배제한 채 철저히 미국과 직거래하는 ‘통미봉남 정책’으로 나올 것입니다.)

Yet the government appears to have excessively high expectations for the U.S.-North Korea summit. Rashly hoping for "Again 2018" could instead result in being excluded from U.S.-North Korea negotiations, suffering a security bypass, or being blindsided. This is a time when proactive consultation with the U.S. and careful management of the situation are needed. (그런데도 정부는 미북 회담에 너무 큰 기대를 갖고 있는 모습입니다. 섣불리 ‘어게인 2018’을 기대했다가 오히려 미북 협상에서 배제된 채 안보 패싱 당하거나 뒤통수를 맞을 수 있습니다. 적극적 대미 협의와 상황 관리가 필요한 시점입니다.)

item.title: Even Nuns Lobby in Washington DC... "If You Don't Understand Lobbying, You Can't Understand the U.S." (수녀님도 로비하는 워싱턴 DC… “로비 모르면 美 이해할 수 없어”)
item.description:
Even Nuns Lobby in Washington DC... "If You Don't Understand Lobbying, You Can't Understand the U.S." (수녀님도 로비하는 워싱턴 DC… “로비 모르면 美 이해할 수 없어”)

In the wake of the Coupang controversy, the importance of outreach to the U.S. — targeting major government agencies and Congress — is being highlighted once again. Domestically, "lobbying" generally conjures up negative images, but in Washington DC, the center of global politics, it is as essential as water and air. K Street, where lobbying firms are clustered, is bustling with government and corporate officials from around the world seeking connections to key figures. Even corporations, universities, and labor unions attacked as "left-wing" by President Donald Trump engage in lobbying to press their demands on influential players and push them through. It's even said that "even nuns lobby." (쿠팡 사태를 계기로 미국의 주요 정부 기관, 의회를 대상으로 한 대미(對美) 아웃리치의 중요성이 다시금 조명 받고 있다. 국내에선 ‘로비(lobbying)’하면 부정적인 이미지를 떠올리는 것이 일반적이지만, 세계 정치의 중심인 워싱턴 DC에선 물과 공기 같은 것이다. 로비 회사가 밀집한 K스트리트는 주요 관계자에 줄을 대기 위해 세계에서 몰려온 정부와 기업 관계자들로 문전성시를 이룬다. 도널드 트럼프 대통령으로부터 ‘좌파’라 공격 받는 기업, 대학, 노동 조합들도 요인을 찾아 원하는 것을 들이밀고 이를 관철시키기 위해 로비를 한다. 심지어 “수녀님들도 로비를 한다”고 한다.)

Woo Jung-yeop, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute and an expert on diplomacy and security, publishes "Access: Washington Moves Through Lobbying" (published by Suyeonsa) on September 1, delving into the fierce competition unfolding on K Street, the world's largest lobbying market. Woo, who has served as executive director of Hyundai Motor's Global Policy Strategy Office and general coordinator of its Washington office, director of strategic planning at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Washington director of the Asan Institute for Policy Studies, is deeply versed in the Washington DC ecosystem and U.S.-Korea relations. He graduated from Seoul National University's business school, earned a master's in public policy from Georgetown University, and a Ph.D. in political science from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. (외교·안보 전문가인 우정엽 허드슨연구소 선임 연구위원이 9월 1일 출간하는 ‘액세스(Access): 워싱턴은 로비로 움직인다(수연사 刊)’는 세계 최대 로비 시장인 K스트리트에서 벌어지는 치열한 경쟁을 다루고 있다. 우 위원은 현대차 글로벌정책전략실장 전무·워싱턴사무소 총괄조정관, 외교부 외교전략기획관, 아산정책연구원 워싱턴 소장 등을 지내 워싱턴 DC 생태계와 한미 관계에 정통한 인물이다. 서울대 경영학과를 졸업하고 미 조지타운대에서 정책학 석사, 위스콘신대 밀워키 캠퍼스에서 정치학 박사 학위를 각각 받았다.)

The author digs into how governments and corporations from around the world gain access to power and reflect their interests in policy. Drawing on his firsthand experience in Washington as a researcher, diplomat, and businessman, he shows how U.S. politics actually operates through the lens of lobbying, noting that "in an era where a single tariff or one line of regulation can decide trillions of won in revenue," "you must understand how the U.S. works to deal with it properly." With a scarcity of Korean-language books on lobbying, this work has already drawn significant interest from practitioners such as diplomats and corporate global affairs staff even before its official release. It has already climbed the rankings in the politics and society categories at major online bookstores. (저자는 세계 각국 정부·기업이 어떻게 권력에 접근하고 이해관계를 정책에 반영하는지 파고들고 있다. 연구자와 외교관, 기업인으로서 워싱턴을 직접 겪은 경험을 바탕으로 로비라는 창을 통해 미국 정치가 실제로 작동하는 방식을 보여주는데 “관세 하나, 규제 한 줄이 수조 원의 매출을 좌우하는 시대”라며 “미국이 어떻게 움직이는지 알아야 제대로 상대할 수 있다”고 했다. 로비를 다룬 한국어로 된 책이 부족한 상황이라 정식 출간 전부터 외교가와 기업 글로벌 대관 실무자 같은 실요자들의 관심이 상당한 상황이라고 한다. 이미 주요 온라인 서점 정치·사회 부문에도 순위권에 올라 있다.)

The Korean government, as well as major corporations, have set up offices in Washington DC and spend considerable sums on lobbying, but a precise understanding of the lobbying ecosystem and how it operates must come first to achieve desired outcomes as a "client." The defense industry, which embeds its projects deeply into district economies to leverage lawmakers, and the case of TikTok crumbling before the geopolitical reality between the U.S. and China, are particularly intriguing. The author argues, "In the end, what prevails in Washington is not the most righteous voice, but the most prepared, most frequent, and best-translated voice," and "that voice becomes policy." Park Yong-man, former chairman of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, called it "a must-read for business leaders and policymakers dealing with the U.S." (한국 정부는 물론 주요 기업들도 워싱턴 DC에 사무소를 차려 로비에 적지 않은 돈을 쓰고 있는데, 로비 생태계와 작동 방식에 대한 정확한 이해가 선행돼야 ‘클라이언트(client)’로서 원하는 결과물을 얻을 수 있다. 사업을 지역구 경제와 깊이 엮어 의원을 상대로 레버지리를 점하는 방산 업계, 미국과 중국 사이의 지정학적 현실 앞에 무너진 틱톡 사례 등이 흥미롭다. 저자는 “결국 워싱턴에서 남는 건 가장 옳은 목소리가 아닌 가장 오래 준비된, 자주 도착한, 잘 번역된 목소리”라며 “그 목소리가 정책이 된다”고 했다. 박용만 전 대한상공회의소 회장은 “미국을 상대해야 하는 기업인과 정책 담당자라면 반드시 읽어야 할 책”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Does the Special Counsel Pave the Way for 'Taming the NIS'?…Talk of a Shake-Up of Hardliners on North Korea (특검이 길 터준 ‘국정원 길들이기’?…대북강경파 물갈이설)
item.description:
Does the Special Counsel Pave the Way for 'Taming the NIS'?…Talk of a Shake-Up of Hardliners on North Korea (특검이 길 터준 ‘국정원 길들이기’?…대북강경파 물갈이설)

With the second comprehensive special counsel probe (Special Counsel Kwon Chang-young) indicting a large number of former government officials of the National Intelligence Service (NIS), including former First Deputy Director Hong Jang-won, on August 19, there are growing observations that the NIS could once again be swept into a vortex of so-called "reform." While large-scale organizational restructuring and personnel shake-ups targeting the military and police have been underway through two rounds of special counsel investigations (the insurrection special counsel and the second comprehensive special counsel) since the December 3 martial law declaration, among NIS officials, only former Director Cho Tae-yong had been standing trial on charges of perjury in his testimony before the National Assembly and the Constitutional Court. However, because Cho was a political appointee of the previous administration and the charges against him were not directly linked to the martial law, there was a strong perception that the NIS had remained relatively untouched by the martial law fallout. But with the second special counsel indicting former Director Cho, former Deputy Director Hong, former Second Deputy Director Hwang Won-jin, and former Planning and Coordination Office Director Kim Nam-woo on charges of performing important duties in the insurrection and abuse of authority under the National Intelligence Service Act, the NIS has now been brought within the frame of having been mobilized for the insurrection. <<> According to reporting by Weekly Chosun, there are predictions in political and bureaucratic circles that the comprehensive special counsel's indictment of former NIS political appointees will trigger a large-scale personnel shake-up. These moves are said to be led by dovish factions on North Korea within the Democratic Party of Korea. A political source told Weekly Chosun, "People classified as North Korea doves within the ruling bloc are calling for pushing back the NIS's hawks—that is, hardliners on North Korea—and turning it into a conciliatory intelligence agency led by doves," adding, "The name of a successor is already being floated among current minister-level officials." However, the source explained that unlike previous administrations when the NIS became entangled in illegal activities and gave grounds for reform, the current NIS lacks sufficient justification for indiscriminate reform, which is a dilemma for the North Korea doves. For this reason, the argument is that because the comprehensive special counsel indicted high-ranking officials who attended the political appointees' meeting during the December 3 martial law—including former First Deputy Director Hong Jang-won (the NIS director, first, second, and third deputy directors, and the Planning and Coordination Office director)—they will use this as justification to push ahead with a sweeping personnel reshuffle. <<> North Korea Engagement Advocates Provide Momentum for Special Counsel Investigation <<> Indeed, on August 19, the comprehensive special counsel indicted four political appointees, including former Director Cho, on charges of performing important duties in the insurrection. Former Director Cho and others are accused of receiving messages from the National Security Office justifying the martial law, passing them on to U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) officials, and collecting overseas reactions to the martial law declaration. Additionally, former Deputy Director Hong is accused of attempting to establish communication channels with the Defense Intelligence Command and the National Police Agency during the martial law, and of ordering the dispatch of personnel to the police agency's situation room. The special counsel also determined that former Deputy Director Hwang's instruction to review plans for dispatching personnel to the martial law command's joint investigation headquarters, and former Director Kim's instruction to select personnel for dispatch to the martial law situation room at the request of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, constituted participation in the insurrection. <<> Among them, former Deputy Director Hong has been most actively rebutting the special counsel's claims. In an interview with Weekly Chosun on August 17, he countered, "I thought I was the only one who received a phone call (on the day of the martial law), but while being investigated by the special counsel, I learned that then-Planning and Coordination Director Kim Nam-woo received a similar call about an hour later," and added, "I see this as strong circumstantial evidence that I was not carrying out the president's order (to 'round them all up')." He further claimed, "Under Director Lee Jong-suk's system, the NIS conducted its own internal inspection, and the conclusion was that 'the NIS was not shaken by the December 3 martial law or insurrection.' In fact, the inspection even found that Director Cho Tae-yong had responded passively, and that inspection document already contained content related to the CIA documents." <<> The special counsel filed the indictment on August 19. But even during the investigation process, suspicions have emerged that details of the special counsel's probe were relayed in real time to parts of the ruling bloc, and that the Democratic Party provided the momentum for the investigation of former Deputy Director Hong. In fact, Park Jie-won, a Democratic Party lawmaker who served as NIS director under the Moon Jae-in administration, appeared on a broadcast about ten days before the special counsel team registered former Deputy Director Hong as a suspect on May 18, and said, "Former Deputy Director Hong will face judicial action." (See Weekly Chosun issue 2910, "How Did Park Jie-won Know About Hong Jang-won's Registration as a Special Counsel Suspect?") On May 7, Park appeared on KBC Gwangju Broadcasting and said, "Probably today or tomorrow (around now), former NIS Deputy Director Hong Jang-won will be summoned by the special counsel," adding, "Based on the significant things he did before he confessed, he will likely be taken into custody." At the time, only a very small number of people even within the special counsel team knew that Hong had become a subject of investigation, yet Park mentioned it on air. At the time, Park told Weekly Chosun in a phone call, "I don't have much to say. I just had a feeling that's how it would go." But Park's remarks became reality. About ten days after his statement, on May 18, the special counsel team registered Hong as a suspect on charges of performing important duties in the insurrection. It is reported that the second comprehensive special counsel team includes a person who was classified as a close associate during Park's tenure as NIS director. This individual is known to have joined the special counsel after retiring from the NIS. <<> Yoon Kun-young, the Democratic Party secretary on the National Assembly Intelligence Committee who served as director of the National Situation Room under the Moon administration, held a press conference at the National Assembly just hours before the special counsel's indictment and claimed that "two years ago, during the December 3 martial law, the Yoon Suk-yeol administration's NIS was aware of the illegal martial law in advance and even prepared for it proactively"—an observation that suggests coordination with the special counsel investigation. <<> During the earlier insurrection special counsel investigation, former Deputy Director Hong was a key witness who helped in the investigation of insurrection charges against former President Yoon Suk-yeol and others. In the impeachment proceedings against Yoon, Hong testified that he "received a phone call from President Yoon telling him to 'round them all up,' and received a list of arrest targets, including politicians, from Yeo In-hyung." Among ruling bloc supporters, there was fierce backlash from the moment it was suggested that Hong, who played a decisive role in stopping the insurrection, could be indicted. In response, Hong appeared on Kim Eo-jun's YouTube channel, known as a mouthpiece for the ruling bloc, to wage a counter-offensive in the court of public opinion. <<> In response, Rep. Yoon held a press conference to argue for the legitimacy of the special counsel's investigation of Hong. Yoon stated, "I directly confirmed that the NIS had a document written in September 2024, three months before the martial law ('Review on Whether Counter-Intelligence Investigation Authority Can Be Exercised During Martial Law'), and further confirmed that this document was systematically distributed to all departments within the NIS, including those handling background checks, counterintelligence, and inspections," adding, "We newly confirmed this time that multiple NIS departments produced review reports to participate in the illegal martial law." He added, "It has been revealed belatedly that the NIS was a ministry that engaged in important duties for the insurrection, no less than the military and police." Yoon emphasized, "Such systematic movements naturally must have been directed from above," and "It is a reasonable inference that the orders came from the political appointees' meeting chaired by Director Cho Tae-yong held at 11:30 p.m. that night." The meeting was attended by former Director Cho, former First Deputy Director Hong, former Second Deputy Director Hwang, former Third Deputy Director Yoon Oh-jun, and former Planning and Coordination Director Kim. In other words, Yoon's claim is that Hong participated in the insurrection at this meeting held before the martial law was lifted. <<> On August 20, Rep. Yoon held another press conference and claimed, "We confirmed that under the Yoon Suk-yeol administration, extensive surveillance of civilians, including politicians, was conducted, and the results were reported up to the president." He then lamented, "It is heartbreaking that the NIS reform, built step by step through three democratic administrations, collapsed like a sandcastle with the emergence of Yoon Suk-yeol," and pointed out, "We must begin NIS reform anew. The first step is to establish the truth." This effectively formalized NIS reform. <<> However, it is reported that the presidential office conveyed negative reactions to the special counsel regarding this investigation of NIS political appointees. This is because, under the second special counsel's logic, conflicts would arise with what the first special counsel indicted, and in that case, it could significantly affect the maintenance of prosecutions against key figures, including former President Yoon Suk-yeol. <<> Did the Special Counsel Engage in De Facto Plea Bargaining with NIS Employees? <<> Controversy is also expected over allegations that some NIS employees engaged in de facto "plea bargaining" with the special counsel to indict former Deputy Director Hong. The comprehensive special counsel views statements made in the names of several bureau directors who indirectly received orders from Hong on the night of December 3, 2024, the day of the martial law, as key evidence of Hong's participation in the insurrection. The special counsel registered 11 current and former NIS employees as suspects in this investigation, of whom 7—excluding the 4 indicted—were not prosecuted. The special counsel stated that it found no charges against former Third Deputy Director Yoon Oh-jun and granted suspended indictment to the other suspects in consideration of their active cooperation with the investigation. During the investigation, Hong's side reportedly requested a face-to-face confrontation with the bureau director who actively cooperated with the special counsel, but the special counsel refused, saying, "How could a confrontation be possible when (Hong) was once his superior?" <<> There is also controversy over the interpretation of the only physical evidence—memos written by working-level officials. These memos were voluntarily submitted to the second comprehensive special counsel during its search and seizure of the NIS in connection with this investigation. In this regard, a former NIS employee familiar with the agency's internal systems told Weekly Chosun, "The number of people who could have actually attended the relevant meeting that night and left memos was around 200 to 250," and "What the special counsel presented was only a tiny fraction of that—just the memos of two people who had transcribed them onto computers." He added, "NIS diaries are required to be returned and destroyed at the end of the year, so the originals often no longer exist, which makes the fact that memos were secured questionable." <<> In response, Hong's legal counsel told Weekly Chosun, "Even the memos of the two people covering the same meeting conflict with each other," noting, "One person wrote 'receive additional liaison officers from the National Police Agency,' while the other wrote the opposite: 'dispatch our personnel to the National Police Agency.'" He argued, "The special counsel is cherry-picking only the interpretations favorable to them from these conflicting records." <<> ▷More articles can be found in Weekly Chosun. (2차 종합특검(특별검사 권창영)이 지난 8월 19일 홍장원 전 국가정보원(이하 국정원) 1차장을 비롯한 지난 정부 국정원 정무직 인사들을 대거 기소하면서 국정원이 다시 한번 ‘개혁’이란 이름의 소용돌이에 빠져들 가능성이 크다는 관측이 나온다. 12·3 비상계엄 이후 2차례 특검(내란특검, 2차 종합특검)으로 군과 경찰을 향한 대대적인 조직개편 및 인적쇄신이 이뤄지고 있는 가운데서도 국정원 인사 중에서는 조태용 전 원장만이 국회 및 헌법재판소에서의 증언 위증혐의로 재판을 받아왔다. 그러나 조 전 원장은 지난 정부 임명직이었던데다, 기소된 혐의가 계엄과는 직접적 연관이 없었다는 점에서 상대적으로 계엄의 무풍지대란 인식이 강했다. 하지만 2차 특검이 조 전 원장을 비롯한 홍 전 차장과 황원진 전 2차장, 김남우 전 기획조정실장을 내란중요임무종사 및 국가정보원법의 직권남용 혐의로 불구속 기소하면서 국정원은 내란에 동원됐다는 프레임 안으로 들어오게 됐다.)

item.title: Ahn Gyu-baek Following in Jeong Seong-ho's Footsteps?…The 'Minister's Dilemma' Looming Over Military Academy Integration (안규백도 정성호처럼?…사관학교 통합에 드리운 ‘장관의 딜레마’)
item.description:
Ahn Gyu-baek Following in Jeong Seong-ho's Footsteps?…The 'Minister's Dilemma' Looming Over Military Academy Integration (안규백도 정성호처럼?…사관학교 통합에 드리운 ‘장관의 딜레마’ )

The offensive against Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-baek, who is leading the government's push to establish the National Defense Military Academy, is intensifying. Minister Ahn is under suspicion of having lied following a meeting on August 13 with the alumni associations of the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies regarding the integration of the military academies. The alumni associations claim that Minister Ahn retracted his statement—in which he said he would "review maintaining the current system"—after the meeting had ended. In response, the Ministry of National Defense maintains that "this is not true." Minister Ahn himself said, "How could I, while integrating the academies, say something like that (about maintaining the current separate system)?" adding, "I fundamentally think it would be difficult." <<> However, both within and outside the military, there are analyses that Minister Ahn, who personally may be keeping the door open to preserving the academies, is pushing the issue forward because, publicly, he is a minister who must support the president's administration of state affairs. This is seen as similar to Justice Minister Jeong Seong-ho, who personally opposed the abolition of the supplementary investigation power but, from his position as minister, ultimately failed to prevent its abolition. <<> A person identified as A, an official from the Air Force Academy alumni association who attended the meeting at the time, told Weekly Chosun, "When we asked Minister Ahn then whether he had any intention to maintain the current system, he directly replied, 'I will consider it as one option with an open mind.'" He added, "Throughout the meeting, he took good notes and listened attentively." He continued, "I presume that after the meeting, the dozen or so defense ministry aides present told the minister something like, 'You should correct your statement.'" <<> Three Service Alumni Associations: "Ahn Gyu-baek Changed His Word" <<> A also said, "Before the meeting began, Minister Ahn and the Army Academy alumni side had a heated exchange over the issue of Minister Ahn's own desertion case." He added, "Minister Ahn got angry, saying something to the effect of, 'Why do you keep playing to the media over matters that haven't even been verified?'" On the integration of the academies, he reiterated, "Minister Ahn clearly stated with his own words, 'I will review maintaining the current system.'" <<> Lee Beom-rim, president of the Naval Academy alumni association, told Weekly Chosun, "At the time, the defense ministry's policy director and spokesperson were also present at the meeting, and I suspect they told the minister something like, 'This could be problematic, so let's correct the statement.'" He noted, "Many people at the meeting directly heard Minister Ahn's remarks." Lee also recalled of Minister Ahn's demeanor, "Before the meeting began, I worried it might be a waste of time, but the minister was more attentive than expected, and the aides around him weren't just pretending to take notes—they were genuinely listening." He added, "In the end, it appears that government officials, including the minister, are moving in step with the president's strong intentions." He concluded, "Separate from that, we will continue to carry out the movement against the integration of the military academies." (정부의 국군사관학교 창설을 주도하고 있는 안규백 국방부 장관에 대한 공세가 점차 거세지고 있다. 안 장관은 사관학교 통합과 관련해 지난 8월 13일 육·해·공군 사관학교 총동창회 측과의 면담 이후 거짓말을 했다는 의혹을 받고 있다. 총동창회 측은 안 장관이 ‘현행 체제 유지를 검토하겠다는 본인의 발언을 면담이 끝난 뒤 번복했다’고 주장하고 있다. 이에 맞서 국방부는 “사실이 아니다”라는 입장이다. 안 장관 본인은 “제가 사관학교를 통합하면서 그런(현재의 분리된) 체제를 유지한다는 말을 할 수 있겠나”라며 “기본적으로 어렵다고 생각한다”고 말했다.)

Despite the alumni associations' rebuttals, the defense ministry counters, "The defense minister met with the alumni association presidents of the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies to listen to their opinions, and said he would hear various views with an open mind during the process of establishing the National Defense Military Academy," adding, "It is not true that he said he would review maintaining the current system." The ministry further stated, "The defense ministry will proceed with the establishment of the National Defense Military Academy as the baseline while reflecting various opinions." Defense Ministry spokesperson Lee Gyeong-ho said on the matter, "It is difficult to disclose the specific contents, discussion points, or wording used at the meeting." <<> However, apart from the ministry's explanation, it appears that Minister Ahn did indeed say directly that he would "review maintaining the current system." Park Pan-jun, president of the Army Academy alumni association, said, "(Minister Ahn) said he had never lied in his life, but later said something to the effect of, 'How can anyone go through life without lying even once?'" <<> Among senior military figures, it is understood that Minister Ahn is merely acting on President Lee's orders, and that his personal stance on the academy integration agenda is quite different. Han Ki-ho, a lawmaker from the People Power Party, likewise said to Minister Ahn during a temporary session of the National Assembly's Defense Committee on August 14, "Minister Ahn, your strength has always been your open-minded attitude and willingness to listen to the other side," adding, "Please return to your former self." Kim Young-soo, head of the National Defense Rights Research Institute, who raised the desertion allegations against Minister Ahn and held a related press conference at the National Assembly, claimed, "The Blue House likely already knows a great deal about Minister Ahn's problems, and because he is aware of this, he is frightened." <<> As a result, not only is the People Power Party strongly calling for Minister Ahn's impeachment, but even within the ruling camp, there is almost no one defending him or offering explanations on his behalf. The only exception has been lawmaker Kim Byung-joo, a former four-star Army general, who said, "It seems like they are trying to attack the individual (Minister Ahn) to undermine the will for the remaining reforms." Some are also criticizing the recent reduction of South Korea-U.S. joint exercises, ordered by U.S. President Donald Trump, as a result of "the government and defense ministry not taking security seriously." <<> ▷For more articles, visit Weekly Chosun. (하지만 군 안팎에서는 개인적으로는 사관학교 유지에 대한 가능성을 열어두고 있는 안 장관이, 공적으로는 대통령의 국정운영을 뒷받침해야 하는 장관이라는 점 때문에 이를 밀어붙이는 것 아니냐는 분석이 나오고 있다. 개인적으로는 보완수사권 폐지에 대해 반대 입장을 보였지만, 장관의 입장에서는 끝내 보완수사권 폐지를 막지 못했던 정성호 법무부 장관과 비슷하다는 것이다.)

item.title: [Interview] Hong Jang-won "The 2025 Me and the 2026 Me Are the Same" ([인터뷰] 홍장원 "2025년의 나와 2026년의 나는 같아")
item.description:
[Interview] Hong Jang-won "The 2025 Me and the 2026 Me Are the Same" ([인터뷰] 홍장원 "2025년의 나와 2026년의 나는 같아")

Hong Jang-won, former First Deputy Director of the National Intelligence Service (NIS), has been recognized as the figure who prevented the situation from escalating by refusing the president's unlawful arrest orders on the day the December 3 martial law was declared. However, the situation was turned on its head in May when the Comprehensive Special Counsel indicted him. Ultimately, on August 19, the special counsel charged the former Deputy Director Hong with engaging in important missions for insurrection. (홍장원 전 국가정보원 1차장은 12·3 비상계엄이 선포된 날 대통령의 위법한 체포 지시를 거부해 사태 확산을 막은 인물로 평가받아 왔다. 그런데 지난 5월 종합특검이 그를입건하면서 상황이 뒤집혔다. 결국 특검은 8월 19일 홍 전 차장을 내란중요임무종사 혐의로 기소했다.)

He is currently a figure on the fence. During last year, when investigations and trials related to the martial law were in full swing, he had to constantly endure criticism from one camp calling him a traitor. From May of this year, when he became the subject of the Comprehensive Special Counsel's investigation, he has been viewed with suspicion by the other camp. The question is whether he is 'a deeply conservative figure at heart' who spent a long time at the NIS—an agency that was once a target of reform for unsavory incidents under previous governments. (그는 현재 경계인이다. 계엄 이후 관련 수사와 재판이 한창이던 지난해에는 한 진영으로부터 변절자란 비판을 끊임없이 받아야 했다. 종합특검의 수사 대상이 된 올 5월부터는 다른 진영에서 의심의 눈초리로 바라보고 있다. 과거 정부에서 불미스러운 일로 개혁의 대상이 됐던, 그 국정원에 오래 몸담아왔던 ‘뼛속까지 보수적 인사 아니냐’는 것이다.)

Former Deputy Director Hong, who had repeatedly declined interview requests, agreed to speak with Weekly Chosun only after the 4th round of questioning by the Comprehensive Special Counsel. A few days before the interview with Weekly Chosun, he appeared on CBS and Kim Ou-joon's YouTube channel to refute the specific charges under investigation by the special counsel. Meeting with Hong at the Weekly Chosun office in Sangam-dong, Mapo-gu, Seoul, on August 17, two days before the indictment, he explained his active engagement in interviews recently by saying, "I'm not claiming that my story is right, but it's the media's job to verify the truth of the special counsel's announcements, so I'm speaking up." He added, "In this situation, actively providing explanations is the only resistance I can offer." This interview focused more on the process of the investigation and its potential repercussions rather than the specific charges being reviewed by the special counsel. Former Deputy Director Hong made remarks suggesting that this special counsel investigation could provide a starting point for forces seeking to shake up the NIS—which had remained an untouchable zone during the martial law—by doing so under the guise of reform. The interview, which lasted about 2 hours and 30 minutes, was attended by Hong's legal representatives: Kim Ik-hyun, the lead attorney, and Cha Yun-seong, an attorney, from the law firm Jiseok. (그간 여러 차례 인터뷰 요청을 거절해왔던 홍 전 차장은 종합특검 4차 조사 이후에야 주간조선 인터뷰에 응했다. 그는 주간조선 인터뷰 며칠 전엔 CBS와 김어준 유튜브 등에 출연해 특검에서 수사하고 있는 구체적 혐의에 대해 반박했다. 기소 이틀 전인 지난 8월 17일 서울 마포구 상암동 주간조선 사무실에서 만난 홍 전 차장은 최근 인터뷰에 적극 임하고 있는 이유에 대해 “내 얘기가 옳다고 주장하는 게 아니라, 특검 발표의 진위를 따지는 건 언론의 몫이니 이야기하는 것”이라면서도 “지금 상황에서는 적극적으로 소명하는 것이 내가 할 수 있는 유일한 저항”이라고 말했다. 이날 인터뷰는 특검 수사를 통해 다뤄지고 있는 혐의보단 수사의 과정이나 이후 있을 파장에 초점을 맞췄다. 홍 전 차장은 이번 특검 수사가 비상계엄의 무풍지대였던 국가정보원을 또다시 흔들려는 세력에게 개혁이란 이름의 흔들기 작업에 단초를 제공할 수 있다는 취지의 발언을 했다. 2시간30분가량 이어진 인터뷰에는 홍 전 차장의 법률대리인인 법무법인 지석의 김익현 대표변호사와 차윤성 변호사가 동석했다.)

- Isn't it true that the JTBC report on May 18 leaked the facts of the charges even before the special counsel notified you of being named as a suspect? "On the day the first report broke, I was having dinner with acquaintances in Pangyo. The first call I got was from an MBC reporter. When I said I didn't know what was going on, they sent me a link to the JTBC article. Even I found it hard to comprehend at the time, so I was quite flustered, wondering what this was all about. Right after the report came out, later that afternoon, the Comprehensive Special Counsel announced that they were naming all senior political appointees at the NIS as suspects. This happened all of a sudden, without any prior interview as a witness or any kind of procedure." (- 특검이 본인에게 입건했다는 통보도 하기 전에 5월 18일 JTBC 보도로 피의 사실이 흘러나온 거 아닌가. “첫 보도가 난 날 판교에서 지인들과 식사하던 중이었다. 처음 전화한 건 MBC 기자였는데, 무슨 상황인지 잘 모르겠다고 했더니 JTBC 기사를 링크로 보내줬다. 그때는 나조차 인지하기 어려운 내용들이었기 때문에 이게 무슨 얘기인지 굉장히 당황스러웠다. 보도가 나온 직후 오후에 곧바로 종합특검에서 국정원 정무직 간부들을 전원 입건한다는 발표가 나왔다. 사전에 참고인 조사나 어떤 절차도 없이 갑작스럽게 이렇게 된 것이다.”)

- The first report contained quite specific details of the alleged charges, and it was also puzzling that there was no rebuttal from you. "A single media outlet ran exclusive reports, and not just once—they kept publishing related stories until the 4th round of questioning was over. There was no separate confirmation from our side. Even though my lawyers explained things thoroughly, I felt that our rebuttals weren't being accepted well." (- 첫 보도에 상당히 구체적인 피의사실이 담겼는데, 반론이 없다는 점도 의아했다. “한 매체가 단독으로, 그것도 한 번이 아니라 4차 조사가 끝날 때까지 계속 관련 보도를 이어갔다. 우리 쪽에는 별도 확인이 없었다. 변호인이 충분히 설명했음에도 반론이 잘 받아들여지지 않았다는 느낌을 받았다.”)

"Special Counsel Only Informed Me of Charges During the 3rd Round of Questioning" (“특검, 3차 조사에서야 피의사실 알려줘”)

During this process, Attorney Kim from Former Deputy Director Hong's side showed the summons issued by the Comprehensive Special Counsel. The 1st and 2nd summons merely stated 'there are matters to inquire about regarding the suspected insurrection case,' without any specific mention of what charges Hong was facing. Attorney Kim said, "Even when we asked what the charges were, they wouldn't confirm, and only in the 3rd summons did they specify the charge: 'Following the orders of NIS Director Cho Tae-yong, mobilizing subordinate departments to execute and justify the December 3 emergency martial law, thereby playing a significant role in the martial law.'" This suggests there were problems with the investigative procedure from the start. (홍 전 차장 측 김 변호사는 이 과정에서 종합특검의 출석요구서를 보여줬다. 1·2차 요구서에는 ‘내란 등 피의 사건에 관하여 문의할 사항이 있다’고 적혀 있었으며 구체적으로 홍 전 차장이 받는 피의 혐의가 무엇인지에 대한 언급은 없었다. 김 변호사는 “피의사실이 뭐냐고 요청해도 확인해주지 않다가, 3차 출석요구서에 가서야 ‘국가정보원장 조태용의 지시에 따라 12·3 비상계엄을 구체적으로 실행하고 정당화하기 위해 소속 부서를 동원해 계엄을 실행하는 등 비상계엄에서 중요 역할을 수행한 혐의’라는 게 명시됐다”고 말했다. 수사 절차부터 문제가 있었다는 주장이다.)

- So you underwent the first round of questioning without even knowing what the charges were. What were the questions like during that first session? "The investigation team's first question was, 'Why didn't you explicitly voice your opposition like former Ministry of Justice inspector Ryu Hyuk or Colonel Cho Sung-hyun?' This is a criminal investigation, not an internal NIS disciplinary review. My lawyer objected, saying they should be asking questions based on the elements of the crime, not questions like that. In the first round, they just asked broadly about what had happened and about CIA matters, and we thought we had explained things thoroughly enough that we left feeling confident. But the very next day, the special counsel issued a briefing saying they had 'given me a chance to defend myself.' That's when I started feeling something was off." (- 피의 사실이 무엇인지도 모르는 상태에서 1차 조사를 받았다는 건데, 그렇다면 1차 조사 때 질문들은 무엇이었나. “수사팀의 첫 질문이 ‘왜 류혁 전 법무부 감찰관이나 조성현 대령처럼 명시적으로 반대를 표명하지 않았느냐’였다. 이건 국정원 내부 직무감찰이 아니라 형사 수사인데, 범죄 구성요건에 맞춰 물어야지 무슨 질문이 이런가 싶어 변호사가 항의했다. 1차 조사에서는 그간 있었던 일과 CIA(미 중앙정보국) 관련 얘기를 평면적으로 물었고, 충분히 설명했다고 생각해 저희도 웃으며 나올 수 있었다. 그런데 다음 날 바로 ‘본인에게 변명할 기회를 줬다’는 취지의 특검발 브리핑이 나왔다. 그때부터 이상하다고 느끼기 시작했다.”)

- On the night of December 3, at the meeting of senior political appointees, you did not share the president's orders with Director Cho Tae-yong. Why not? "That night at 10:53 PM, I received the president's order to 'arrest them all, support the Defense Intelligence Command.' Right after that, I spoke with Defense Intelligence Commander Yeo In-hyung and learned the list of people to be arrested. From that moment, I judged that something was wrong and decided to refuse the president's order through inaction. In fact, no NIS employee left the building to arrest anyone on the list. However, at the meeting of senior political appointees, I did not even disclose that I had received orders from the president. Because I couldn't predict how the other senior officials would react. At the time, I decided not to stir up unnecessary discord, but I thought I should report separately to the agency head after the meeting of subordinate department heads concluded, so I had a private meeting with the Director." (- 12월 3일 밤 정무직 회의에서 대통령의 지시를 조태용 원장에게 공유하지 않았다. 왜인가. “그날 밤 22시53분 대통령으로부터 ‘싹 다 잡아들여, 방첩사를 지원하라’는 지시를 받았고, 곧이어 여인형 방첩사령관과 통화하며 체포 대상자 명단을 알게 됐다. 그 순간부터 뭔가 문제가 있다고 판단했고, 부작위(不作爲)로 대통령의 지시를 거부하기로 했다. 실제로 국정원에서 체포자 명단에 있는 사람을 잡으러 청사 밖으로 나간 직원은 아무도 없었다. 다만 정무직 회의에서는 대통령으로부터 지시를 받았다는 사실 자체를 알리지 않았다. 다른 정무직들이 어떻게 반응할지 예측할 수 없었기 때문이다. 당시 괜히 분란을 만들지 않겠다고 판단했고, 대신 산하 부서장 회의가 끝난 뒤 기관장에게는 따로 보고해야겠다고 생각해 원장을 독대했다.”)

"The Only Physical Evidence the Special Counsel Has Is Memos from Working-Level Officials" (“특검이 가진 물적 증거는 실무관 메모뿐”)

Regarding the charges against former Deputy Director Hong, the first thing that became public was the allegation that he instructed subordinates to explain the purpose of the martial law to the CIA. According to the special counsel, these instructions were confirmed through statements from NIS employees currently under investigation and two memos from working-level officials secured during the special counsel's seizure and search of the NIS. Attorney Kim argued that none of these memos were written by Hong himself, and even the two memos contain statements that passed through multiple levels, not from the department head who directly heard Hong's remarks. He added that, in fact, many parts of these memos were actually favorable to Hong, but the special counsel was only focusing on portions that could be used against him. (홍 전 차장의 피의사실과 관련해 가장 먼저 알려진 건 CIA에 계엄 취지를 설명하라는 지시를 부하직원들에게 했다는 것이다. 이러한 지시는 현재 수사대상인 국정원 직원들의 진술과 특검의 국정원 압수수색을 통해 확보한 실무자들의 메모 2개를 통해 확인했다는 것이 특검 측의 입장이다. 김 변호사는 이 메모 중에 홍 전 차장이 직접 작성한 것은 없으며, 2개의 메모조차도 홍 전 차장의 발언을 직접 들은 부서장이 아닌 여러 단계를 거친 발언이 담겨 있다고 주장했다. 심지어 이 메모 내용에는 홍 전 차장에게 유리한 정황도 많았는데, 특검은 이 중 홍 전 차장에게 불리하게 작용할 수 있는 부분들만 보고 있다고 덧붙였다.)

- Were the working-level memos presented as physical evidence handwritten or digital records? "First of all, none of those memos were written by me directly. They are hearsay records that passed through three to four levels. The chain goes: senior political appointees meeting → meeting of subordinate department heads → working-level meeting chaired by a bureau director → and then transcribed onto a PC by the person in charge. I believe this is the kind of record whose accuracy regarding what I actually said can be legitimately questioned." (- 물증으로 제시된 실무진의 메모는 수기로 작성된 건가, 디지털 기록인가. “일단 그 메모들 중 내가 직접 작성한 건 없다. 3~4단계를 거쳐 전달된 전문(傳聞) 기록이다. 정무직 회의 → 산하 부서장 회의 → 국장 주재 실무관 회의 → 담당자를 거쳐 PC에 옮겨 적는 과정을 거친다. 이게 정말 내가 한 말이 맞는지 의문을 제기할 수 있는 종류의 기록이라고 본다.”)

- It was said these memos were secured through a seizure and search. Was it done through voluntary submission? How did they come to find them? (Attorney Kim Ik-hyun answered this question on his behalf) "Whether it was the audit team or the inspection team, they conducted their own forensic analysis and then voluntarily submitted the materials. I heard that during the process of voluntary submission, when the NIS compiled and submitted materials to the special counsel, they had already selected and submitted only the materials unfavorable to Deputy Director Hong. The evidence that came to the special counsel through the NIS's voluntary submission process itself was classified to include only damaging items. (The memos themselves) don't just contain what Hong said; they also include what department heads said, what the working-level officials discussed among themselves, and even additional notes they added because they found certain parts interesting." (- 그 메모들은 압수수색을 통해 확보했다고 했는데, 임의제출 방식이었나? 어떻게 발굴해냈다고 하던가.(이 질문에 대한 답변은 김익현 변호사가 대신했다) “감사팀이든, 감찰팀이든 포렌식을 자체적으로 해서 임의제출을 했다. 임의제출 과정에서 국정원이 무슨 자료를 만들어서 특검에 제출할 때 이미 그 자료들 중에 홍장원 차장에게 불리한 자료를 선별해서 제출했단 얘기를 들었다. 국정원에서 임의제출의 과정을 거쳐서 특검으로 왔던 증거물들 자체가 불리한 것들로만 분류되어 있다는 것이다. (메모 자체도) 홍 차장이 얘기한 것만 들어간 게 아니라 부서장이 얘기한 것도 들어가고, 또 자기들(실무관)끼리 협의한 내용도 들어가고, 심지어는 자기가 관심 있는 부분을 메모에 추가로 옮겨서 적어놓은 내용까지 포함돼 있다.”)

- Did the special counsel investigate the employees who wrote the memos? "We can't know that." (- 메모를 작성한 직원을 특검이 조사했나. “우리는 알 수 없다.”)

- What was the intent behind your instruction at the separate meeting of subordinate department heads to 'not be agitated and focus on their core duties'? "At the senior political appointees meeting (attended by the NIS Director, First, Second, and Third Deputy Directors, and the head of the Planning and Coordination Office), the Director gave only one instruction: 'Compile and report by tomorrow morning what the NIS can do under emergency martial law.' So at the meeting of subordinate department heads, I only said things like 'Don't be agitated, focus on your core duties' and 'The Director is curious about this, so let's put together a summary by morning.' I gave no specific instructions about what to do that night. What the department heads discussed—like strengthening counterintelligence activities or requesting more police liaison officers—was just an extension of their usual routine work." (- 별도로 이뤄진 산하 부서장 회의에서 ‘동요하지 말고 본연의 업무에 집중하라’고만 한 말의 의도는 뭔가. “정무직 회의(국가정보원장, 1차장, 2차장, 3차장, 기획조정실장이 참여하는 회의)에서 원장이 지시한 건 딱 하나, ‘내일 아침까지 국정원이 비상계엄하에서 뭘 할 수 있는지 정리해 보고하라’는 것뿐이었다. 그래서 산하 부서장 회의에서도 ‘동요하지 말고 본연의 업무에 집중하라’ ‘원장님이 이런 걸 궁금해 하시니 아침까지 종합하자’는 취지의 말만 했을 뿐, 그날 밤 뭘 하라고 구체적으로 지시한 게 없다. 부서장들이 얘기한 내용도 방첩 활동 강화, 경찰 파견관 충원 요청 등 평소에도 늘 하던 통상 업무의 연장선이었을 뿐이다.”)

- I've heard that after the president's order to you, similar (arrest) orders may have been given through other channels outside the NIS. "I thought I was the only one who received a call, but during the special counsel investigation, I learned that Kim Nam-woo, the then-head of the Planning and Coordination Office, received a similar call about an hour later. You could see that as an indication that since I wasn't carrying out the order, the president directed someone else. However, while it's true there are signs that personnel were prepared for dispatch to the martial law command as a result, there is absolutely no basis to conclude that the NIS as an organization provided manpower and funds to support the insurrection. Rather, I see this as strong circumstantial evidence that I was not carrying out the president's 'arrest them all' order." (- 대통령이 홍 전 차장에게 지시한 이후 국정원 외에 다른 라인으로도 (체포)지시가 내려간 정황이 있었다고 들었다. “나만 전화를 받은 줄 알았는데, 특검 조사를 받으면서 나 말고도 김남우 당시 기조실장이 1시간쯤 뒤 유사한 내용으로 전화를 받았다는 사실을 알게 됐다. 내가 이행하지 않으니 다른 사람에게 지시했다고 볼 수 있는 대목이다. 다만 그 결과로 계엄사에 파견 인력을 준비한 정황이 있는 건 맞지만, 이걸 국정원이 조직적으로 인력과 자금을 지원해 내란에 관여했다고 볼 근거는 전혀 없다. 오히려 이건 내가 (싹 잡아들이라는) 대통령의 지시를 이행하지 않고 있었다는 강력한 정황이라고 본다.”)

- What about the incident involving the delivery of explanatory materials about the martial law to the CIA? "That happened on the morning of December 4, and I had no prior knowledge of it. The National Security Office delivered the document to the Director, and I understand the Director instructed the bureau chief in charge. I was bypassed in that chain of command." (- CIA에 계엄 관련 설명자료를 전달한 건은 어떻게 된 일인가. “12월 4일 아침의 일로, 나는 사전에 몰랐던 사안이다. 안보실에서 원장에게 문건을 전달했고, 원장이 담당 국장에게 지시한 것으로 알고 있다. 나는 그 라인에서 패싱됐다.”)

- Usually, in a situation like this, wouldn't foreign intelligence agencies or embassies in Korea request explanations about the situation? I imagine there were many such requests on the night of the 3rd. Isn't responding to those also part of the First Deputy Director's duties? How did you handle that? Were there any instructions during that process that could be misconstrued? "The special counsel actually asked me about that. During the meeting of subordinate department heads on the night of the 3rd, the bureau director in charge of overseas affairs asked, 'Intelligence agencies from various countries in Seoul keep calling to check on the situation—how should we respond?' At that point, I knew about the illegal situation because of the president's call, but the employees knew nothing. The intelligence cooperation (intel-sharing) channels, which were set up to prepare for situations even worse than war, military provocations, nuclear tests, or missile launches, had to be maintained no matter what. So I said to maintain them. Then they asked, 'So what do we tell them?' That's when I was at a loss for words. So I only gave the principled answer that 'intelligence cooperation channels must be maintained under any circumstances.' But I couldn't give specific instructions on what to say. Because I already knew about the president's arrest orders, I judged that if I hastily gave instructions, there was a risk that illegal content would be passed along directly. So I just said, 'Have the overseas analysis bureau assess the situation further and put something together.'" (- 통상적으로 이런 비상사태가 벌어지면 국내에 들어와 있는 해외정보기관이나 대사관에서 상황에 대한 설명요청이 오지 않나. 아마도 3일 밤 그런 요청들이 많이 왔을 것 같은데, 이에 답하는 것도 1차장의 업무다. 어떻게 지시했나? 이 과정에서 오해의 소지가 있는 지시는 없었나. “안 그래도 특검에서 그걸 물었다. 3일 밤 당시 산하 부서장 회의에서 해외담당 국장이 ‘서울에 있는 각국 정보기관들에서 계속 확인 전화가 오는데 어떻게 대응할까요’라고 물어온 일은 있다. 나는 대통령 전화를 받아 불법적 상황을 알고 있었는데, 직원들은 아무것도 몰랐던 때 아닌가. 전쟁 군사도발, 핵실험, 미사일 발사 그보다 더한 상황을 대비해서 만들어 놓은 정협(정보협력) 라인은 어떻게든 유지를 해야 한다. 그래서 유지하라고 했는데, (직원들이) 그럼 어떻게 답을 합니까라고 물어봤다. 그때 딱 말문이 막혔다. 그래서 ‘정보협력 라인은 어떤 상황에서도 유지해야 한다’는 원론적인 답만 했다. 다만 구체적으로 뭐라고 답변하라는 지침까지는 하지 못했다. 대통령의 체포지시를 이미 알고 있었기 때문에, 섣불리 뭔가를 지시했다가 자칫 불법적인 내용이 그대로 전달될 위험이 있다고 판단했기 때문이다. 그래서 ‘해외분석국에서 상황을 좀 더 파악해서 정리해달라’고만 답했다.”)

- The special counsel announced regarding the CIA document delivery that 'the Deputy Director was briefed on everything and approved and countersigned it.' You've emphasized in media interviews that this wording itself is problematic. "Under the National Intelligence Service Act, the Deputy Director's role is to assist the Director; the Deputy Director has no authority to approve or countersign the Director's decisions. The authority to decide and command rests solely with the Director. The phrasing 'the Deputy Director countersigned what the Director decided' is inherently nonsensical." (- 특검은 CIA 문건 전달 건에 대해 “차장이 모든 걸 보고받고 승인·재가했다”고 발표했다. 이 표현 자체에 문제가 있다고 언론 인터뷰에서 강조했다. “국가정보원법상 차장은 원장을 보좌하는 지위이지, 원장의 결정에 대해 승인이나 재가를 할 권한 자체가 없다. 결정권과 지휘권은 원장에게 있다. ‘원장이 결정한 걸 차장이 재가했다’는 워딩 자체가 성립하지 않는 얘기다.”)

Contradictions Between the 1st Insurrection Special Counsel and the 2nd Comprehensive Special Counsel (1차 내란특검과 2차 종합특검의 모순)

With the indictment of former Deputy Director Hong, various interpretations are now clashing between the 1st Insurrection Special Counsel and the 2nd Comprehensive Special Counsel, and there is ample room for those indicted by the 1st special counsel to challenge the legality of the investigation or the credibility of Hong's statements. A prime example is the question of when the insurrection ended. The 1st special counsel views the insurrection as ending on December 4 when the National Assembly voted to lift martial law, but the 2nd special counsel sees it as ending on December 14 when the National Assembly passed the impeachment motion against former President Yoon Suk-yeol. This ten-day gap is significant because it vastly expands the pool of potential suspects. On this point, Attorney Kim pointed out, "Military personnel who withdrew before the insurrection ended, who are now on trial for insurrection, could be charged with attempted insurrection, and even former President Yoon could potentially be an attempted insurrectionist." (홍 전 차장이 기소되면서 1차 내란특검과 2차 종합특검 사이에서 여러 가지 해석이 충돌하고, 1차 특검으로 기소된 사람들이 특검 수사의 불법성이나 홍 전 차장의 진술 신빙성을 문제 삼을 수 있는 소지가 다분하다. 대표적인 것이 내란 종료 시점이다. 1차 특검은 12월 4일 국회 계엄 해제 의결 시점을 내란 종료로 보지만, 2차 특검은 12월 14일 국회에서 윤석열 전 대통령에 대한 탄핵소추안이 통과됐을 때로 보고 있다. 이 열흘의 간격은 피의자의 범위가 훨씬 늘어난다는 점에서 중요하다. 이와 관련해 김 변호사는 “종료되기 전에 철수한 군인 등 지금 재판을 받고 있는 내란 피고인들은 내란 미수가 되고, 더 나아가면 윤석열 전 대통령도 내란 미수범이 될 수 있다”고 지적했다.)

- The special counsel seems to be trying to push the end date of the insurrection to December 14. "This is the most difficult part to understand. Four existing judicial bodies and even Supreme Court precedent have all treated December 4, when martial law was lifted, as the end of the insurrection. But since the CIA document delivery happened on the morning of December 4, if they keep that end date, this matter becomes entirely unrelated to the insurrection from the start. The only way to implicate me is to push the end date to the 14th. If they're moving the goalpost for the end of the insurrection just to indict me, there has to be some intent behind it—there's no other reason to go that far." (- 특검이 내란 종료 시점을 12월 14일로 보고 늦추려 하고 있다. “이게 가장 이해하기 어려운 지점이다. 기존 4개 사법기관과 대법원 판례까지 12월 4일 계엄 해제를 내란 종료 시점으로 봐왔다. 그런데 CIA 문건 전달이 12월 4일 아침에 이뤄진 일이라, 이 시점을 그대로 두면 이건 애초에 내란과 무관한 사안이 된다. 이걸 14일로 늘려야만 나를 걸 수 있게 되는 구도다. 나를 기소하기 위해 내란 종료 시점 자체를 움직이려 한다면, 이건 뭔가 의도가 있지 않고서야 그렇게까지 할 이유가 없는 문제다.”)

- You've already been investigated by four judicial bodies—the police, the prosecution's special investigation unit, the Corruption Investigation Office for High-ranking Officials (CIO), and the 1st Insurrection Special Counsel—and they all concluded that you refused the president's unlawful orders. The Comprehensive Special Counsel's investigation contradicts those conclusions. "I was dismissed right after the martial law, but the NIS side expressed gratitude a few times, calling my decision a courageous one that blocked the president's unlawful orders. This is a matter that was already reviewed by four judicial bodies and the NIS's own internal inspection, all concluding there was no problem. Now, for the Comprehensive Special Counsel to reach a different conclusion, they would either have to have found new facts that all previous investigations missed, or the NIS would have had to conceal something knowingly. Neither is plausible by any common sense." (- 경찰, 검찰 특수부, 공수처, 1차 내란특검까지 이미 4개 사법기관에서 조사를 받았고, 대통령의 불법 지시를 거부했다는 결론이 났었다. 종합특검 수사는 이 결론과도 배치된다. “저도 계엄 직후 경질되긴 했지만, 국정원 측에서는 대통령의 불법 지시를 막은 용기 있는 결단이었다는 평가로 감사인사를 몇 번 받았다. 이미 4개 사법기관과 국정원 자체 감찰까지 거쳐서 문제없다는 결론이 나온 사안이다. 그런데 종합특검이 이제 와서 다른 결론을 내리려면, 기존 조사들이 다 놓친 새로운 사실을 찾아냈거나 국정원이 알고도 숨긴 것 중 하나여야 하는데, 둘 다 상식적으로 받아들이기 어렵다.”)

- Why do you think the Comprehensive Special Counsel is going this far all of a sudden? "The Defense Intelligence Command has been disbanded. The prosecution's investigative powers were split. The military and police were dealt heavy blows by this insurrection. Among all of them, the NIS was the only one that remained untouched. But if the conclusion is flipped so that the NIS Deputy Director who refused the president's unlawful orders is now seen as having participated in the insurrection, I think that has to be viewed as a problem aimed at the NIS as an institution itself. By framing me the way the Comprehensive Special Counsel wants, they're dragging the entire NIS into it." (- 종합특검이 갑자기 왜 이렇게까지 한다고 보나. “방첩사는 해체됐고, 검찰은 수사권이 분리됐고, 군경도 이번 내란으로 큰 타격을 받았다. 이 가운데 유일하게 무풍지대로 남아있던 게 국정원이었는데, 대통령의 불법 지시를 거부한 국정원 차장이 오히려 내란에 가담한 것으로 결론이 뒤집힌다면, 이건 국정원이라는 조직 자체를 향한 문제로 봐야 한다고 생각한다. 종합특검이 원하는 대로 저에게 뒤집어씌움으로써 국정원이 통째로 달려 들어가는 것이다.”)

- Isn't the fact that the NIS, which has been embroiled in various scandals, did not join the illegal martial law proof that the agency has changed from the past? "The Defense Intelligence Command has been disbanded, and the military and police suffered significant damage from this insurrection. The public security system that has been protecting national security is going through a tremendous ordeal right now. So the only survivor in the national security apparatus is the NIS, and now they're trying to label that surviving institution as one that was involved in the insurrection, aren't they?" (- 그동안 여러 불미스러운 일에 휘말렸던 국정원이 불법계엄에 가담하지 않았다는 건 그동안 국정원이 과거와는 달라졌다는 방증 아닌가. “방첩사가 해체됐고, 군경이 이번 내란으로 상당히 큰 타격을 받았다. 지금 국가의 안보를 지키고 있던 공안 시스템이 굉장히 큰 수난을 겪고 있는 상황이다. 그러면 국가 공안 시스템에서 유일하게 생존한 건 국정원인데, 지금 그 생존한 국정원에 대해서 내란에 관여한 기관이라고 평가를 하려고 하는 것 아닌가.”)

As Former Deputy Director Hong said, there are currently no cases of long-serving NIS employees being punished in connection with this insurrection. Until the indictment on August 19, only former Director Cho Tae-yong had been convicted in the first trial for perjury before the National Assembly and the Constitutional Court. (홍 전 차장의 말처럼 현재 국가정보원에 오랜 기간 근무했던 직원들이 이번 내란으로 인해 처벌받은 사례는 없다. 지난 8월 19일 기소 전까지는 조태용 전 원장만이 국회와 헌법재판소에서 위증한 혐의로 1심에서 유죄를 선고받았다.)

"Trapped in a Frame, Like a Fly Caught in a Spider's Web" (“프레임에 갇혀 거미줄에 걸린 파리 같다”)

- Could this now lead to another conspiracy theory that 'the NIS was organizationally involved in the insurrection'? "Sometimes questions are posed with the underlying assumption that 'the NIS must have been involved.' I'm not sure that's the right approach to looking at this. We should judge based on the facts that exist, but if you push the narrative that 'someone—maybe not me, but surely someone—must have received a call and been involved,' the next step inevitably becomes 'the NIS must be reformed, must be disbanded.' I don't think such conspiratorial thinking serves national security." (- 이제 ‘국정원이 조직적으로 내란에 관여했다’는 또 다른 음모론으로 번질 수도 있지 않나. “질문의 의도 자체가 ‘국정원이 개입됐을 것’이라는 전제에 맞춰져 던져지는 경우가 있다. 그런 의심을 갖고 사안을 바라보는 게 올바른 접근법인지 모르겠다. 있는 사실을 갖고 판단해야 하는데, ‘누군가는, 예를 들어 내가 아니었어도 누군가는 전화를 받았을 거고 개입돼 있었을 것’이라는 식으로 몰아가면, 결국 다음 단계는 ‘국정원을 개혁해야 한다, 해체해야 한다’는 수준으로 가버린다. 그런 음모론적인 시각은 국가 안보에 도움이 안 된다고 생각한다.”)

- During the impeachment phase, you were criticized as a 'traitor.' Now you're being accused of the exact opposite—being an insurrection participant. What have you thought while going through all of this? "In 2025, I felt anger. I told the truth, but why was I accused of lying? But this time is different. Being told 'You are a criminal, you engaged in insurrection missions' is deeply humiliating. Even though I didn't do it, the situation itself makes me feel ashamed, and I sense people around me looking at me as if to say, 'If the special counsel, a state judicial body, is going this far, maybe you really did do something.' I can't show what's inside me. It's something I have to prove, and that's why I'm now talking about all sorts of things. It feels like I'm trapped in a frame, like a fly caught in a spider's web... I've explained things as thoroughly as I could over four rounds. And if, despite the legal reasoning being flawed and the facts being different, they push forward with an indictment, isn't that something I have to resist for the sake of my own human rights, my own dignity, everything? The problem is, I just can't understand why they're going this far. But the Hong Jang-won of 2025 and the Hong Jang-won of 2026 are the same person. What I want to say through media interviews is not that my story is right—I believe it's the media's job to carefully verify the truth. Whether I say 'Please look at this fairly' or 'No, that's not how it is,' what I'm doing is presenting my position." (- 탄핵 국면 때는 “변절자냐”란 비판을 받았고, 지금은 정반대로 내란 가담자로 몰리고 있다. 이 모든 과정을 겪으며 든 생각은.“2025년에는 분노가 있었다. 사실대로 말했는데 왜 거짓말을 했다고 하냐는,. 그런데 이번엔 다르다. ‘너는 죄인이다, 내란 임무에 종사했다’는 말은 사람을 굉장히 위축시킨다. 하지 않은 일인데도 이 상황 자체가 부끄럽게 느껴지고, 주변에서도 국가 사법기관인 특검이 저렇게까지 하는 걸 보면서 ‘너 정말 그랬던 거 아니냐’는 시선을 보내는 걸 느낀다. 내 속을 드러내 보일 수도 없고, 내가 입증해야 하는 부분인데 그러다 보니 지금 뭐 별거를 다 막 얘기하고 있다. 뭔가 지금 프레임에 갇혀 가지고 거미줄에 걸린 파리처럼… 네 번에 걸쳐 충분히 설명할 수 있을 만큼 했는데, 그게 법리적으로도 맞지 않고 사실관계가 다른데도 불구하고 (기소를) 강행한다면 그거는 제 스스로의 인권이든, 자존심이든 모든 것을 위해서 저항해야 하는 거 아닌가? 그런데 문제는 왜 이렇게까지 하는지 이해가 잘 안 된다. 하지만 2025년의 홍장원과 2026년의 홍장원이 다르지 않다. 언론하고 인터뷰하는 과정에서 얘기하고 싶은 건 내 얘기가 옳다가 아니고 진위 여부는 잘 따져보는 것이 언론의 일이라고 생각한다. ‘잘 봐 주세요’ 혹은 ‘아니에요 그렇지 않아요’라고 하든 내 입장을 소명하는 거다.”)
